description: Alaska historic extreme events library is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Alaska Center for Climate Assessment & Policy; University of Alaska Fairbanks | International Arctic Research Center; Alaska Climate Research Center. Alaska Center for Climate Assessment and Policy and Alaska Fellows have compiled a library of historical weather and climate events that significantly impacted Alaskans. They combed newspapers, disaster declarations, agency briefings and other sources to create a suite of over a dozen outreach products that clearly communicate each meteorological event and its associated impacts. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Changing Seasons, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Flooding – General, High Winds, Landslides, Severe Winter Weather. Assets: Economy, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
